headline: CPI vs PCE:
Which Inflation
Number Does
the Fed Use?
slides.subtitle:
Two price gauges, one clear winner
for the Fed.

slides.title: In One Sentence
slides.big: CPI is the inflation number in the headlines. PCE is the one the Fed targets.
slides.body: The Fed's 2% goal is defined using PCE prices, from the Bureau of Economic Analysis.

slides.title: How They Differ
items: PCE: broader spending, incl. health care (BEA).
PCE adjusts as shoppers switch products.
slides.footer: Both track prices, with different recipes.
slides.disclaimer: For informational purposes only. Not investment advice.

slides.title: Why It Matters to You
slides.body: CPI sets Social Security COLAs and shapes everyday price talk. PCE guides Fed rate decisions, which reach loans and savings.

slides.title: Remember This
items: The two often differ by a bit.
slides.disclaimer: For informational purposes only. Not investment advice.
